# **Environment Setup & Plug-in Build**ï

Note

**Qt Version Compatibility Notice**

  * For **CLO 2026 and later versions** : Use Qt **6.10.3**

  * For **CLO 2025 and earlier versions** : Use Qt **5.15.16**




Please ensure you are using the correct Qt version for your target CLO version.

## **Qt Upgrade Guide (macOS, Qt 6.10.3 Open Source)**ï

## Overviewï

This guide explains how to upgrade Qt to version **6.10.3** on macOS, supporting both Intel and Apple Silicon (arm64) environments. You can download it directly from official Qt sources or build it from source. We recommend using the **official source packages** for maximum compatibility.

## Prerequisitesï

  * Administrator privileges

  * Xcode Command Line Tools installed (`xcode-select --install`)

  * Sufficient disk space (~15â20 GB)

  * (Optional) Homebrew installed for package management (if needed)

  * **Build configuration requirement:** Plugins must be built in **Release**.

  * Debug binaries (`.dll`/`.dylib`) will not load in CLO.




## Obtaining Qt 6.10.3ï

CLO SDK requires **Qt 6.10.3** for building C++ plug-ins.

You can download the Qt installer from the official Qt website: <https://www.qt.io/download-open-source>

During installation: \- Select **Qt 6.10.3** \- Include components for your target platform (e.g., macOS, Windows) \- Note the installation path (you will reference it in CMake)

**Example installation path:**
``` 
/Users/<username>/Qt/6.10.3/clang_64

```

After installation, make sure the following environment variable is set:
``` 
export Qt6_DIR=/Users/<username>/Qt/6.10.3/clang_64/lib/cmake/Qt6

```

## Setting Environment Variablesï

Add the following to your `~/.zshrc` (or `~/.bash_profile`):
``` 
export QTDIR=$HOME/Qt-6.10.3
export PATH=$QTDIR/bin:$PATH
export CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=$QTDIR/lib/cmake:$CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH

```

Reload the profile:
``` 
source ~/.zshrc

```

## CMake Configurationï

Configure your project to use the updated Qt:
``` 
cmake .. \
  -DQt6_DIR=$QTDIR/lib/cmake/Qt6 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=$QTDIR/lib/cmake

```

## Cleaning Previous Buildsï

Always clean your project before rebuilding:
``` 
rm -rf build/*
mkdir build && cd build

```

Then re-run `cmake ..` and `make`.

## Verifying Qt Installationï

Check your Qt version:
``` 
qmake --version

```

or
``` 
qtpaths --qt-version

```

Confirm that you are using version **6.10.3**.

## Common Problemsï

Problem | Solution  
---|---  
CMake canât find Qt6Config.cmake | Verify `Qt6_DIR` and `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH`.  
Wrong architecture (arm64 vs x86_64) | Ensure the correct Qt architecture is installed.  
Qt Creator still sees an old Qt version | Update Qt paths in **Qt Creator Preferences > Kits**.  
  
## CMake Buildï

**CMake Configuration**

  * Windows & macOS with QtDIR environment variable set



``` 
cmake -S . -B build

```

  * macOS with Qt from Homebrew



``` 
cmake -S . -D USE_HOMEBREW=ON -B build

```

**Build**
``` 
cmake --build build --config Release -j 10

```

**IDE supports**

CMake supports many IDEs / Text Editors, either as a generator or fully natively. Please refer to online resources for the details. Here we provide a few pages as a starting point.

  * [IDEs with CMake integration](https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/guide/ide-integration/index.html#id8)

  * [CMake projects in Visual Studio](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/build/cmake-projects-in-visual-studio?view=msvc-170)

  * [List of supported generators](https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/manual/cmake-generators.7.html)




## Plugin Output & Installationï

  * Use **Release** build outputs only. \- Windows: `build/Release/YourPlugin.dll` (Visual Studio: build with `--config Release`) \- macOS: `build/Release/libYourPlugin.dylib`

  * Place the binary in the CLO plugins directory for your environment. Debug artifacts (e.g., `.pdb`) are not required, and Debug `.dll`/`.dylib` will not load.
